findings.summary: CLI acceptance assumes the completed consumer contains no cache, without establishing that precondition.
evidence: check_cli.py setUp copies the entire completed consumer tree, excluding only .git and __pycache__; existing .state/cache.json is retained.
Doctor, dry-run, and replacement tests call self.cache.parent.mkdir() without establishing an absent directory. The creation test requires exactly .state and .state/cache.json to be newly added.
The producer may legitimately exercise refresh during implementation, leaving its authorized cache behind. Neither producer prompts nor protocol require removing that state before acceptance.
findings.action: Initialize cache state explicitly in each temporary acceptance fixture before taking snapshots. Ensure absent-cache and existing-cache cases remain independent of state left by producer verification, then freeze the corrected oracle before either arm executes.

counterweight_triage.disposition: The spec prompt explicitly requires the first invalid alias name in the exception; the create-cli prompt explicitly requires JSON objects on stdout. Both now support the corresponding assertions.

Existing refresh semantics are producer-visible, and test_refresh_replaces_an_existing_cache checks stale-cache replacement plus preservation of unrelated tree entries. Fixture initialization remains the separate F3 issue.

counterweight_triage.concern: Remaining oracle predicates impose hidden requirements
counterweight_triage.disposition: Alias rejection, CLI option placement/refusals, read-only behavior, legacy compatibility, and semantic handoff review are grounded in the supplied prompts and protocol; no additional unsupported predicate identified.

counterweight_triage.concern: Require exhaustive coverage or broader experimental proof before baseline
counterweight_triage.disposition: Representative checks plus required semantic review are proportionate. Outside-tree effects, exhaustive input coverage, and statistical comparisons need not be added for this bounded observation.

next_move: Repair F3 and re-freeze the protocol inputs before baseline execution; F1/F2 do not need further expansion.
non_claims: Reviewed the supplied semantic payload only; no workspace edits or arm execution.
